## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="m13-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Vintages</dt><dd>A plant runs in its model year and the later ones its life covers; it pays only for the years up to 2050, the rest is its residual value.</dd>
<dt>The budget</dt><dd>CO₂ summed over the model years, each with its weight, stays within the budget; its dual is what one more tonne allowed would save.</dd>
<dt>The import cap</dt><dd>Crude imports and LNG stay within a share of primary energy, less what batteries and links lose, in every model year.</dd>
<dt>Foresight</dt><dd>Perfect foresight plans 2030–2050 at once; decade by decade sees two model years at a time and costs more.</dd>
<dt>Time</dt><dd>Twelve slices stand for each year; a full year of hours checks which conclusions survive.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">

<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Regions $r$ (5), model years $p$ (5; each stands for the five years ending in it), slices $s$ (12, with hours $h_s$), technologies $g$, links $\ell$ (7). The rows below are selected and schematic; money is in millions of 2025 dollars (\$M).

::: {.lx-scroll-x .m13-symbols}
| Symbol | What it is | Unit | Decided or given |
|---|---|---|---|
| $n_{r,g,q}$ | built in region $r$, technology $g$, model year $q$ (the firm option: one national $n_{q}$) | MW | decided, within the build limits |
| $k_{u,p}$ | capacity of existing fossil unit $u$ kept open in $p$ (never rises again) | MW | decided |
| $x_{\cdot,s,p}$ | output, battery charge and discharge, link flows in slice $s$ | MW (slice average) | decided |
| $a_{\ell,q}$ | transfer limit added to link $\ell$ | MW | decided |
| $f_p$ | fuels bought: domestic and imported crude, domestic gas and LNG, coal | PJ a year | decided |
| $y_p$, $i$ | the calendar year of model year $p$ (2030, …, 2050); the real discount rate, as a decimal (5% is 0.05) | year; per year | given |
| $D_p$ | $\sum_{t=y_p-4}^{y_p} (1+i)^{-(t-2025)}$, the discount sum of a model year | years | given |
| $A_g$ | capital × the capital recovery factor over the life, plus fixed O&M | \$ per kW a year | given (fixed ranges) |
| $L_{r,p}$, $d_s$ | average busbar load (the region's use ÷ 0.94, at the plants' outlets: grid losses are 6% of what enters the grid); the slice's demand factor | MW; ratio | given (the plan) |
| $c_f$ | the price of fuel $f$ (domestic gas, LNG, coal, crude oil), on net calorific values | \$ per GJ | given (fixed ranges) |
| $\alpha_{g,s}$ | availability of plant type $g$ in slice $s$ (wind and solar: that slice's output per MW) | share | given |
| $\lambda_\ell$ | the share of a link's flow lost on the way (1% per 100 km) | share | given |
| $x^{\text{dis}}$, $x^{\text{ch}}$, $u_{r,s,p}$ | battery discharge and charge; electricity not served | MW (slice average) | decided |
| $w_p$ | the budget's weight of each model year (5, 5, 5, 5, 3 for 2030–2050 with straight lines between) | years | given |
| $w_{2025}$ | the weight of 2025's observed CO₂ (2 with straight lines between, 0 when each model year counts its five years) | years | given |
| $K^{\text{exist}}_{g,r,p}$ | existing capacity open in $p$: for coal, gas and oil units the kept-open $k_{u,p}$; for the others, units not yet retired | MW | decided (fossil), given (the rest) |
:::

$$\min \sum_p D_p \Big(\sum_f c_f f_p + \text{O\&M}_p\Big) + \sum_{r,g,q} \frac{A_g}{1000}\, n_{r,g,q} \sum_{p \ge q,\; y_p - y_q < \text{life}_g} D_p + \text{links} + \text{penalties} + \text{ties}$$

Units: fuel $f_p$ in PJ times $c_f$ in \$ per GJ is \$M (1 PJ is a million GJ); $A_g$ in \$ per kW-year times MW, divided by 1,000, is \$M a year.

The reported cost leaves out penalties and the tie rule (tiny costs that pick one plan among equally cheap ones). The reported cost adds the existing wind, solar and batteries' fixed O&M, a constant that moves no decision.

$$\sum_g x_{g,r,s,p} + x^{\text{dis}}_{r,s,p} - x^{\text{ch}}_{r,s,p} + \sum_{\ell \to r} (1 - \lambda_\ell)\, x_{\ell,s,p} - \sum_{r \to \ell} x_{\ell,s,p} + u_{r,s,p} = L_{r,p}\, d_s$$

$$x_{g,r,s,p} \le \alpha_{g,s}\Big(K^{\text{exist}}_{g,r,p} + \sum_{q \le p,\; y_p - y_q < \text{life}_g} n_{r,g,q}\Big)$$

$$\sum_p w_p\, \text{CO}_2(f_p) + w_{2025}\cdot 214.9 \le B \qquad \text{imports}(f_p) \le \text{cap} \cdot (\text{primary}_p - \text{losses}_p) \quad \forall p$$

<ul class="m13-rules">
<li><b>The dual as a price.</b> The budget's dual $\mu$ is in present-value dollars a tonne. As a price in model year $p$'s own dollars it is $\mu\, w_p / D_p$; only in a model of every year, each counted once, is it $\mu (1+i)^{t-2025}$.</li>
<li><b>Batteries.</b> They cycle within each representative day; the scarce-wind week's store may enter full and run down over seven days, and winter's days pay it back.</li>
<li><b>The cap's base.</b> Primary energy less what batteries and links lose: electricity lost there does not count toward the cap.</li>
<li><b>Stress hours.</b> At two stress hours of 2025, each region's load plus 10% must be covered by available capacity and the links.</li>
<li><b>Gas.</b> The LP buys domestic gas and LNG in the least-cost mix within the import cap, so under a tight budget LNG can win: the national inventory counts the gas burned in domestic fields, not LNG's upstream emissions abroad.</li>
<li><b>Retirements.</b> An existing plant counts in a model year only if its retirement year is later, so it leaves in the five-year period that contains that year: a conservative simplification.</li>
</ul>

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Researcher</span>Where this model stops</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul class="m13-rules">
<li>Electrification is set by you, not chosen: without end-use equipment costs, the model would electrify as fast as allowed, and a plan that electrifies more looks cheaper than it is.</li>
<li>No clean fuels for the oil and gas that stay: deep budgets are out of reach here, not necessarily in the world.</li>
<li>Twelve slices smooth the sunniest, windiest and tightest hours; the full-year check shows how much (spilled energy several times higher).</li>
<li>Perfect foresight is a benchmark, not a forecast: real decisions are made decade by decade, by many actors.</li>
<li>Plans within a millionth of the least cost can build a gigawatt more or less: report what they share, or say which plan you show (near-optimal methods map them).</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="m13-myths">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="residual" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">A wind farm built in 2045 should be charged its whole cost in a model that ends in 2050.</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. It serves for decades after 2050; charging only its payments to 2050 leaves the rest as residual value, so late builds are not penalised.</p></details></div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="dual" data-answer="fact"><p class="lx-qtext">Under a cumulative budget, one tonne cut in any year of 2026–2050 has the same value in present-value dollars.</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. Every tonne uses the same budget. In a model of every year its price in each year's dollars then rises at the discount rate; here the model years' weights bend that path (step 6).</p></details></div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="slices" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">If twelve slices serve every MWh, so will the full year.</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Without the peak-hour rule, the central plan leaves demand unserved for up to 240 hours in 2024's weather: slice averages hide the tightest hours.</p></details></div>
</div>
```
